headings.font: Cabinet Grotesk, Outfit, or Clash Display
headings.style: premium modern sans-serif, large bold headlines, tight hierarchy, oversized typography in the hero. Tracking tight (-0.02em to -0.04em).

body.style: clean, modern, highly legible. High contrast white/off-white against dark backgrounds.

accents.style: used for micro-stats, overlines, and technical labels. Uppercase, tracking wide (0.1em to 0.2em).

visual_enhancers.glassmorphism: Subtle glassmorphism for navbars and floating elements. Must use background color (e.g., bg-black/60) with backdrop-blur-xl and a delicate 1px inner stroke (border-white/10). No purely transparent backgrounds over content.
visual_enhancers.gradients: Soft, subtle radial gradients (e.g., green/lime accent) in the background. Maximum 20% opacity. Avoid full-screen generic linear gradients.
visual_enhancers.texture: Subtle grain/noise overlay on the entire body to eliminate digital flatness and create an editorial/cinematic feel.
visual_enhancers.borders: 1px solid borders with 10% white opacity. Use nested radii (e.g., parent rounded-2xl, child rounded-xl).

layouts.general: Desktop-first mentality but fully responsive. High breathing room (Tailwind p-12, p-16, p-24). Mobile-first CSS grids with optical alignment.
layouts.hero: Kinetic layout. Large oversized headline, tight leading. Visually secondary 3D element (Spline/R3F) confined strictly to a hero boundary, never overlapping text or CTAs.
layouts.portfolio: Masonry or strict CSS grid for cinematic thumbnails. Large scale (no tiny cards). Hover reveals play button/video snippet.
layouts.cards: Services and Case Studies should use solid dark surfaces or subtle gradients (not generic SaaS cards). Consider 'Grid Borders' (The Technical Look) for case studies.

motion.scroll: Lenis smooth scrolling is mandatory for premium momentum.
motion.reveals: Framer Motion for scroll reveals. Text lines masked and revealed from bottom to top (kinetic typography).
motion.hover_states: Image scale on hover for portfolio (overflow-hidden wrapper). Buttons should have smooth background/color transitions.
motion.marquee: One slow, editorial marquee for 'Building in Public' or social proof (very slow, smooth drift, gap-32).
motion.3d_element: Lightweight, subtle 3D character (via Spline) floating or rotating gently in the hero.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure text over images/gradients meets 4.5:1 ratio using dark overlays.
accessibility.testing: All interactive elements (buttons, links, form inputs) must include data-testid (e.g., data-testid='hero-cta-button', data-testid='contact-form-submit').
accessibility.focus: Clear focus states with the primary accent color.

3d_libraries.recommended: @splinetool/react-spline for the 3D character (lightweight, easily embeddable, looks premium) or React Three Fiber if custom geometry is needed. Do not let it block interactions.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a React (.jsx/.js) frontend using Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, and Lucide React icons. You have .js files not .tsx files.
Do not use generic Shadcn cards out of the box for the portfolio or case studies; strip Vercel-like styling to create dark, borderless, or fine-1px-bordered premium components.
Navbar MUST have a solid/semi-solid background (e.g., bg-black/60) with backdrop-blur-xl and NEVER be fully transparent over content.
Use @splinetool/react-spline for the 3D character in the Hero. Confine it to a specific div on the right/bottom corner of the hero so it NEVER overlaps the primary text, CTAs, or the header.
Use framer-motion for kinetic typography (line reveals) in the hero, and staggered fade-ups for the services/portfolio grids.
Portfolio needs a filter mechanism (All, Short Form, Long Form, Motion Graphics, AI, Social Media) and a cinematic grid layout.
Implement a project detail modal using framer-motion AnimatePresence or a dedicated dialog, containing a video player placeholder, client, category, overview, and tools.
Add 'sonner' for toast notifications in the Contact form.
Include specific placeholders where real data is missing. DO NOT invent fake names, clients, or awards. Use 'Placeholder Client', 'Placeholder Testimonial', etc.
Use the exact provided URLs for the imagery in the designated sections.
Ensure all interactive components and key text have 'data-testid' properties.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur).
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Use sonner for toasts, located in /app/src/components/ui/sonner.js or equivalent JS.
